claim: Issue #228 step 2 (the Curator's order): the committed stream's M1.S.2/.3/.4/.5 family survives because klt's via_pad_trim pass structurally cannot touch it, measured on the committed slice at the pin. The pass already did everything it can do here: it dropped the one redundant pad (the power via array's merged M1 pad, fully wire-covered in all placements; report cells_touched 1, pads_trimmed 1, pads_left 1). The surviving pad - the router's standard V1 via cell VIA_VIA12, one 18 x 22 nm pad at 8,905 placements - fails the drop test at 8,237 of 8,905 placements (the pad protrudes past routed M1 exactly at the wire-endpoint placements where it is the connection, so it is not redundant), and fails the shrink test by construction: the pad is a strict subset of the pass's shrink floor (V1 cut 18 x 18 nm sized by the pass's 5 nm enclosure bound = 28 x 28 nm), so pad & (cut sized 5 nm) == pad and the pass's own strict-reduction test rejects any change. The deck's M1.S.* markers are placement-specific pad-to-neighbor spacing pairs: 270 of the 305 marker bboxes interact with a surviving pad placement (35 are pad-free routed-wire tip pairs). Both trim tests are uniform across every placement of a cell and neither reads deck spacing, so a pad that is required at one placement and too close to a neighbor at another cannot be edited at all. The upstream disposition is 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#4508 (open): trim protruding VIA_* M1 pad tips to clear M1.S.2-5. Its acceptance criteria's shrink-to-minimum-enclosure fallback is present at the 0.9.2 pin and is measured here to be a no-op for this pad; the family therefore stands recorded by name and count with an open upstream issue. No committed file changed in this pass; the committed-stream measurement of record moves from r5 to this record byte-identically.

shrink_test_on_surviving_pad.reading: the shipped pad already sits at or inside the pass's minimum-enclosure floor - the floor derives from the deck's V1.M1.EN.1 5 nm side bound, a rule the deck itself lists as unmodeled (not checked), so no deck-legal smaller pad exists for the pass to produce; the pad is at the LEF VIARULE minimum

m1_s_marker_attribution.bucket_reading: per the deck's Table 3.12.1 the buckets are tip/topology-dependent: S.4 (tip-to-tip, both edges < 24 nm, 31 nm required) dominates at 193 - the 18 nm pad tip against a routed wire tip; S.5 (mixed tip widths, 31 nm) 64; S.3 (both tips 24..36 nm, 27 nm) 32; S.2 (tip-to-side, 25 nm) 16

via_pad_trim_analysis.conclusion: The family survives by construction, not by misconfiguration. The pass is a redundancy minimizer: drop a pad only when every placement of its cell is fully covered by wire; shrink only to the fixed V1-enclosure floor and only when connectivity is preserved at every placement; no test reads deck spacing; edits are per-cell master shapes, never per-instance. The router's standard V1 pad fails the first test at 92.5% of placements (it is the connection there), cannot pass the second (it is already inside the floor), and its M1.S.* violations are pad-to-neighbor spacing pairs that exist only at specific placements. No request field at this pin changes any of that. The upstream gap for the missing capability is 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#4508 (open, ASAP7: trim protruding VIA_* M1 pad tips to clear M1.S.2-5): its acceptance criteria's shrink-to-minimum-enclosure fallback is present at the 0.9.2 pin and measured above to be a no-op for this pad, so the remaining upstream work is the protruding-tip policy plus live evidence. The r2-r4 records cite #4495 (closed 2026-11-16 as a no-op) for this family; #4508 is its open successor and the family's live disposition from this record on.
via_pad_trim_analysis.upstream_comment: The generic measured facts (shrink-floor containment of a VIARULE-minimum pad; all-placements-uniform edits cannot address placement-specific spacing; pin 0.9.2 state of #4508's acceptance criteria) were posted to 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#4508 on 2026-11-17, no design-specific detail.
